subject: Art & Design
title: Fallingwater: A House Over a Waterfall
description: Learn Fallingwater: A House Over a Waterfall in one minute.

hook.text: Frank Lloyd Wright built a house directly over a waterfall. Not beside it. Over it. You hear water beneath your feet.

buildup.text: The Kaufmann family wanted a house with a view of the waterfall. Wright gave them one that became the waterfall.

discovery.text: Cantilevered concrete trays extend over the stream without visible supports. The house floats above nature.

twist.text: Engineers warned the cantilevers would fail. They sagged within years. Structural repairs continue to this day.

climax.text: Despite structural issues, it's considered the best example of organic architecture — building as part of landscape.

punchline.text: Wright didn't place a house in nature. He made nature part of the house.

quiz.question: What makes Fallingwater an example of organic architecture?
options: The building integrates directly into the natural landscape over a waterfall
It's built entirely from organic materials
It generates its own electricity from the water

details.summary: Fallingwater (1935) by Frank Lloyd Wright is a house built directly over a waterfall in rural Pennsylvania. Reinforced concrete cantilevers extend dramatically over the stream, making the waterfall part of the living experience. It is widely considered the greatest work of American architecture.
details.whyItMatters: Fallingwater proved that architecture could merge completely with nature rather than merely sitting beside it. The house doesn't overlook the waterfall — it inhabits it — redefining the relationship between built and natural environments.
takeaways: Concrete cantilevers extend the house over a waterfall
The building merges with its natural site rather than overlooking it
Widely considered the greatest work of American architecture

faq.question: Is Fallingwater structurally sound?
faq.answer: The cantilevers began sagging almost immediately — Wright underestimated structural loads and resisted his engineer's advice. Major reinforcement with post-tensioned cables was completed in 2002. The house is now stable but required significant structural intervention.

faq.question: Can you visit Fallingwater today?
faq.answer: Yes. It's a National Historic Landmark in Mill Run, Pennsylvania, operated by the Western Pennsylvania Conservancy as a museum. Guided tours run year-round. It's a UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of Wright's collective architectural works.
